explanation: Q1 filters rows where c2 = c3, then selects distinct c2 as ID and orders by ID. Q2 filters rows where c3 = c2, then selects distinct c2 as ID and orders by c2. The difference lies in the WHERE clause condition, which affects which rows are considered for the DISTINCT operation.
counterexample: INSERT INTO table1 (c1, c2, c3, c4) VALUES (1, 10, 20, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO table1 (c1, c2, c3, c4) VALUES (2, 20, 10, '2023-01-02');
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have rows where c2 = c3 and c3 = c2, but the values of c2 and c3 are different. This will cause Q1 and Q2 to return different results due to the different WHERE clause conditions.
